summary: Exploring intent before implementation is well motivated for ambiguous work, but it should be adaptive: ask only questions whose answers can change scope, design or acceptance.

points.text: ClarifyGPT supplies direct evidence that targeted questions can improve code-generation accuracy when the initial request admits multiple interpretations.
Writing resolved assumptions, non-goals and acceptance criteria creates a reviewable contract and prevents the implementation agent from silently choosing an interpretation.
Question value should be decision-based: if no plausible answer changes the plan or test oracle, asking adds friction without reducing risk.
Requirements-quality research is heterogeneous, so teams should measure rework, clarification latency and escaped expectation defects instead of assuming a longer specification is better.
